solution.title: Q4 · Competitive Lotka–Volterra
solution.problem: $x'=x(4-x-2y)$, $y'=y(3-x-y)$ on $x,y\ge0$. Equilibria, types, eigen-data at the interior point, and the limits from $(3,1.5)$ and $(1,0.5)$.

steps.note: (2, 1) is an equilibrium: it lies on x + 2y = 4 and x + y = 3. The others: (0,0), (4,0), (0,3).
Interior eigenvalues ≈ 0.5616 and −3.5616: opposite signs, so (2, 1) is a saddle.
λᵤ = (−3 + √17)/2 has eigenvector (1, −(1 + √17)/8): first row of (J − λI)v = 0.
(0, 0): J = diag(4, 3). Both positive: unstable node.
(4, 0): J = [[−4, −8], [0, −1]], triangular, eigenvalues −4 and −1: stable node.
At x = 3 the separatrix (stable manifold of the saddle, integrated backward) is at y = 1.3739. (3, 1.5) is above it, so it tends to (0, 3).
At x = 1 the separatrix is at y = 0.5837. (1, 0.5) is below it, so it tends to (4, 0).
